record.paper_title: Billiard Dynamics: A Survey with the Emphasis on Open Problems
record.original_question: Let ℘(n) be the parameter space of Euclidean n-gons up to scaling, equipped on each combinatorial component with the corresponding Lebesgue measure and normalized to a probability measure λ. Let 𝓔(n)⊂℘(n) be the set of ergodic n-gons. Is λ(𝓔(n)) positive?

evidence.quote: Let λ be the probability measure on P(n), whose components are the corresponding Lebesgue measures.
By [49], the set E(n) ⊂ P(n) of ergodic n-gons is residual in the sense of Baire category [57].

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For each integer $n\ge 3$, let $\mathcal{P}(n)$ denote the parameter space of Euclidean $n$-gons considered up to similarity (i.e., up to translation, rotation, and positive scaling). The space $\mathcal{P}(n)$ decomposes into finitely many combinatorial components, each of which is a finite-dimensional smooth manifold carrying a natural Lebesgue measure class; let $\lambda$ be the probability measure on $\mathcal{P}(n)$ whose restriction to each component is the normalized Lebesgue measure (with components weighted to give total mass one).

For a polygon $P\in\mathcal{P}(n)$, consider the billiard flow on the unit tangent bundle of $P$: a point mass moves in straight lines at unit speed inside $P$ and reflects elastically (angle of incidence equals angle of reflection) at the boundary, with trajectories hitting vertices left undefined. The billiard flow preserves the Liouville (phase-volume) measure. Call $P$ ergodic if its billiard flow is ergodic with respect to this Liouville measure. Let $\mathcal{E}(n)\subset\mathcal{P}(n)$ be the set of ergodic $n$-gons.

Question: Is $\lambda(\mathcal{E}(n))>0$?
artifact.status_search_result: It is classical (Kerckhoff–Masur–Smillie and subsequent work) that the set of ergodic polygons is residual (Baire-generic) in $\mathcal{P}(n)$, and recent results establish weak mixing on dense $G_\delta$ subsets. However, no result establishes that the set of ergodic polygons has positive Lebesgue measure in any combinatorial component; this remains a well-known open problem in the field of polygonal billiards.

status_evidence.title: Weakly Mixing Polygonal Billiards
status_evidence.snippet: There exists a G_δ dense set of polygons such that the billiard flow is weakly mixing with respect to the Liouville measure.
status_evidence.claim: Ergodicity/weak mixing for polygonal billiards is known only on Baire-generic sets, with measure-theoretic genericity left open.

status_evidence.title: Recent advances in open billiards with some open problems
status_evidence.snippet: Key open questions include: Is the billiard flow in every irrational polygon ergodic? Is it weakly mixing? Is it mixing?
status_evidence.claim: The measure of the ergodic locus in polygon space is not settled in the literature.
